rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality expanded blastocyst and the provided 3AA grade, but it over-interprets image details (e.g., exact ICM location/nuclear appearance, possible 4AA/hatching) that may not be clearly visible.

Integrates age, endometriosis, ovarian reserve, prior biochemical pregnancy, sperm quality, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality in a clinically meaningful way, though some claims are stronger than the data support.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear link from embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis; minor issues include speculative adjustments and an unsupported euploidy estimate tied to low oocyte yield.

Mostly aligned with Gardner grading and general IVF principles, but includes some nonstandard or weakly supported statements (e.g., idealizing >10 mm lining, implying sperm parameters reduce paternal aneuploidy risk, anti-inflammatory adjuncts without clear indication).
Provides only limited practical next steps in the visible portion; recommendations are broad and somewhat vague, with little concrete transfer management or future-cycle planning detail.
